desc: Orders, circulars, or loose-leaf manuals announcing major policy and procedure changes issued by agency heads.
retention: Program directives: retain permanently — offer to Archives in 5-year blocks when 20 years old. Routine administrative directives: destroy when superseded.
notes: Mixed: program directives are permanent; routine directives are destroyed when superseded. Supporting case files scheduled separately.

desc: Pamphlets, reports, leaflets and manuals related to management projects.
retention: Record copy with supporting papers: submit a disposition request to the Archives. Working papers: see Item 9.

desc: Inventories, disposal authorizations, schedules and reports documenting the agency's records programs.
retention: Basic documentation: destroy when the related records are destroyed, transferred, or no longer needed. Extra copies / routine correspondence: destroy when no longer needed.

desc: Record copy of agency-created forms with instructions and inception documentation.
retention: Record copy: destroy 5 years after the form is discontinued. Working papers: destroy when the form is discontinued.

desc: Copies of reports, analyses and feeder reports on management improvement.
retention: Submit a disposition request to the Archives.

desc: Statistical reports of agency records holdings required by the Office of Public Records.
retention: Reports prepared by designated offices: destroy when 3 years old. Records held by other offices: destroy when 1 year old.

desc: Memoranda and reports documenting project assignments and completion.
retention: Destroy 1 year after the year the project is closed.

desc: Case files for each agency report — clearance forms, directives and discontinuance documentation.
retention: Destroy 2 years after the report is discontinued.

desc: Project background records — studies, analyses, notes, drafts and interim reports.
retention: Destroy 6 months after final action on the project, or 3 years if no action is taken.

desc: Correspondence, reports and records on forms, mail, microforms and records-management surveys.
retention: Destroy when 6 years old (earlier if superseded).

desc: Records relating to interagency, advisory and internal committees and sponsored conferences.
retention: Establishment/policy records and final reports (liaison or sponsor copy): submit a request to the Archives. Other copies and other committee records: destroy when 3 years old.
notes: Mixed: policy/establishment records go to Archives review; routine copies are destroyed at 3 years.

desc: Organizational charts, reorganization studies, functional statements and agency histories.
retention: Retain permanently; offer to the Archives when 5 years old.

desc: Studies for technology or equipment, including cost-benefit analyses of proposed information systems.
retention: Destroy 5 years after the study is completed.

series: Expenditure Accounting General Correspondence & Subject Files
desc: Correspondence or subject files of units responsible for expenditure accounting, on their internal operations and administration.
retention: Destroy when 2 years old.

desc: General accounts ledgers showing debit and credit entries and reflecting expenditures in summary.
retention: Destroy 10 years after the close of the fiscal year.
notes: Accounts with unsettled claims require the D.C. Controller's written approval before disposal.

desc: Allotment records showing the status of obligations and allotments under each authorized appropriation.
retention: Destroy 10 years after the close of the fiscal year.

desc: Records serving as posting and control media, subsidiary to the general and allotment ledgers.
retention: Original records: destroy when 3 years old. Copies: destroy when 2 years old.

desc: Records for civilian personnel under the District Salary Act — qualifications, performance ratings and personnel actions.
retention: Post-1920 records: 75 years after date of birth (or 60 years after the earliest document if the birth date is unknown), or 5 years after separation, whichever is later. Transfer to the Records Center 30 days after separation.
notes: Folders created before January 1, 1921 must be offered to the D.C. Archives before disposition.

desc: Official personnel folders for Police, Firemen's Salary Act and Teachers' Salary Act employees.
retention: 75 years after date of birth (or 60 years after the earliest document), or 5 years after separation, whichever is later. Transfer to the Records Center 90 days after separation.

desc: Documentation for applicant evaluation and selection — applications, rankings and selections.
retention: Destroy 2 years after selection or cancellation.

desc: Letters or telegrams offering appointments.
retention: Accepted offers: destroy immediately (filed in the OPF). Declined offers: destroy after another selection is made.

desc: Classification appeal case files.
retention: Destroy 3 years after the case is closed.

desc: Performance ratings (O.P. Form 12) and supporting materials.
retention: Outstanding/Unsatisfactory ratings: permanent in the OPF. Satisfactory/Excellent: destroy when 3 years old or superseded. Appeals: destroy 3 years after settlement.
notes: Mixed: extreme ratings stay permanently in the OPF; routine ratings are destroyed at 3 years.

desc: P.O. Form 1 documenting employment actions.
retention: Chronological file: destroy when 2 years old. Other copies: destroy when 1 year old.

desc: Public-official and employee financial disclosure reports.
retention: Retain and dispose per statute.
statute: D.C. Official Code § 1-1462 (1981 ed.) — superseded; now § 1-1162.24 et seq. (BEGA)
notes: Legal basis: the retention period is set by statute, not by administrative need. Cited as of the schedule; the modern ethics statute is administered by the Board of Ethics and Government Accountability.

desc: Complaint files — correspondence, reports, decisions and hearing records.
retention: Destroy 4 years after resolution by the agency, the EEOC or a court.

desc: Race and sex employment statistics (aggregate).
retention: Destroy when 5 years old.
notes: Aggregate demographic statistics, not individual records.

series: Alcohol and Drug Abuse Program Records
desc: Records from the planning and coordination of the employee substance-abuse program.
retention: Destroy when 3 years old.

desc: Arbitration correspondence, forms and background papers.
retention: Destroy 5 years after final resolution of the case.

desc: Correspondence on employee training participation and availability.
retention: Destroy when 5 years old or when superseded/obsolete, whichever is sooner.

desc: Witness statements, hearing reports, findings, original decisions and appeal records.
retention: Destroy 3 years after the case is closed.

desc: Case files for disciplinary and non-disciplinary removals, suspensions, leave actions and reductions in force.
retention: Destroy 4 years after the case is closed.

desc: Forms, reports and medical/investigatory records of on-the-job injuries.
retention: Destroy when 5 years old.
notes: Sensitive — contains medical and injury records.
